title: Cancer dying as a more legible but still uneven terminal decline

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source trajectory-axis synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no clinical validation, no individualized prognosis.
limitations: Public sources support vocabulary, course-shape context, family-language routing, and review gates only.
Trajectory labels must not be rendered as diagnosis, prognosis, hospice eligibility, treatment advice, insurance logic, or timing estimate.
Individual course depends on clinical context, care setting, comorbidities, personal goals, local law/policy, and the care team.

moment.plain_scene: A family recognizes a more continuous decline in advanced cancer—less eating, less waking, more weakness—but still cannot know the exact timing.

content_layers.observation_text: A family recognizes a more continuous decline in advanced cancer—less eating, less waking, more weakness—but still cannot know the exact timing.
content_layers.source_synthesis: NCI and trajectory literature support that advanced cancer often has a clearer terminal phase than organ failure or frailty, while last-days changes do not occur in everyone.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record exists to make trajectory visible without converting it into a prediction engine. It should help readers understand why deaths do not all follow the same curve, while protecting clinical, legal, and ethical boundaries.

what_this_is_not: not a countdown for cancer death
not evidence that a person is definitely in the final hours
uncertainties: Cancer can have crises, rallies, hemorrhage risk, infections, and treatment-related complications.
The same sign can appear earlier or later in different people.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface may help a reader recognize the course-shape words they heard and understand why timing can be uncertain. It must route medical, urgent, eligibility, legal, and treatment questions to qualified local care.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Practitioner surfaces should collect diagnosis labels, actual observed course, setting, reversibility uncertainty, family expectations, language used by clinicians, and moments when trajectory framing helped or harmed.
language_notes: Avoid countdown phrasing unless quoted from a source and framed as uncertain.
Do not collapse palliative care, hospice, comfort care, conservative care, and giving up.
Preserve family phrases like “better then worse,” “not bouncing back,” “just old age,” and “what are they dying of?” without treating them as diagnoses.
When a term sounds like eligibility or law, keep it jurisdiction- and care-team-bound.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the trajectory axis. Requires palliative/condition-specific clinical review, prognosis-language review, accessibility review, and lived-witness testing before any public surface uses it.

safety.identifiability_risk: low_from_public_sources_but_medium_if private illness course, age, rare disease, location, or exact timeline enters
safety.medical_advice_risk: medium_to_high_if trajectory language is rendered as diagnosis, treatment advice, hospice eligibility, or timing prediction
safety.cultural_sensitivity: medium because illness labels, family expectations, disability, age, and place of death are culturally and socially shaped
safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not diagnosis, not prognosis, not hospice eligibility guidance, not a treatment recommendation, not death confirmation, not emergency triage, not insurance or benefits guidance, and not a substitute for clinicians, palliative care, hospice, disease specialists, emergency services, mental-health support, legal/policy review, or the person’s care plan.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through palliative, condition-specific clinical, disability/accessibility, ageism/equity, prognosis-language, and family-search testing. Remove countdown, deterministic, eligibility, or abandonment language.

review.legal_or_policy_review_state: needed_if hospice eligibility, certification, benefits, advance-care-planning, or death-certificate language is rendered
review.bereavement_review_state: needed_for family expectation, guilt, and aftermath language
